headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network tools make prompt injection, data leakage, and capability conflicts plausible by default; compliance risk is lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads and writes workspace files, uses MCP, and has no default self-isolation; marketingskills also reads/writes files and builds on shared context. That creates a plausible file-based instruction bridge even though no direct injection channel is documented. The interaction is inferred from both profiles, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or shared skill files, injected instructions can cross from B to A.
IF Cline parses file content or MCP payloads as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable shared skill directories between agents.
Review any file or MCP content before Cline consumes it.
Use read-only mounts for B's context files.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all cross-agent file inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys, while marketingskills reads and writes shared skill/context files. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or screenshots can be exposed through B's outputs or file access. The profiles do not show PHI or a third-party exfiltration loop, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem, B can read artifacts Cline writes.
IF Cline stores screenshots or secrets in workspace files, B can surface them in downstream content.
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate directory.
Move secrets out of shared workspaces.
Restrict B to non-sensitive files only.
Audit workspace outputs before reuse.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Cline also modifies git state and runs shell commands. With shared-state via filesystem and no locking shown, concurrent edits can clobber files or git history in default use. This is a direct overlap on mutable resources, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF either agent edits git state without coordination, history or working tree corruption can occur.
mitigations: Run agents in separate clones.
Serialize write operations manually.
Pause one agent before the other edits git state.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
requires-engineering: add file and git locks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code and browser-derived outputs, and marketingskills is designed to build on shared context. That makes it plausible that B treats A's output as input without verification, causing propagated mistakes. There is no evidence B autonomously sends emails or commits actions, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF B consumes Cline-generated text as authoritative context, errors can cascade into later outputs.
IF Cline's browser-derived claims are copied into B without review, misinformation can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review between agents.
Ask B to cite or verify A's claims.
Keep A's outputs in a draft-only folder.
Limit B to summarization, not action-taking.
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and touch code or marketing content, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. The only concrete compliance concern is that Cline handles model-provider API keys and browser screenshots, which could matter if shared with B's file context. Because the mismatch is not documented, this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace, retention and residency obligations may diverge.
IF Cline screenshots or secrets are copied into B-managed files, policy scope can expand.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared folders.
Review retention settings for both tools.
Store secrets in a separate vault.
Use redacted copies for marketing work.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries.
